seal.statement: Each of the services, nodes and replica_operations system tables has one decoder module (<table>-row-decoder.js exporting decode<Table>Row) that turns a stored-shape row into a frozen canonical object with named states: closed domains (services status and raft_role, nodes status and connection_state, replica_operations type, status and workflow_step) refuse an unknown stored value, SQL NULL decodes to a named absent state, a column the row lacks is a typed refusal, and a partial SELECT decodes through a named projection declared once beside the query that yields exactly the projection's named fields and a projection marker; the existing per-table normalisers (normalizeServiceRow, normalizeReplicaRow, normalizeCensusServiceRow, normalizeCurrentVoterServiceRow, normalizeNodeRow, the column decoding of ReplicaOperationRepository#rowToOperation, normalizeReplicaOperationRecord, normalizeOperationProgressRecord, readOperationWorkflowRecord, normalizePublicationOperationWorkflowRecord and the routed display normalisers) are folded into the decoders so one version of each decoding exists and their call sites read decoded objects; and the budget gains the measuring rows system_table_raw_column_reads_outside_decoder (reads of a table's own columns outside its decoder and write builders, capped one-way at the measured count) and one row per directory group (rebalancer, control-plane, node, admin, query, partition; target 0) that the system-table-decoded-reads-* quests drive to zero; behaviour is unchanged.

text: Lead rulings 2026-11-08 22:10 CET on the implementer's questions. (1) Partial rows in the system-table cache: the cache merge holds complete rows. On insert of a row the cache does not hold, the merge applies the stored schema's declared column defaults exactly as the SQL table would (NULL for nullable columns, the declared DEFAULT for NOT NULL columns with one) and REFUSES an insert that omits a NOT NULL column without a default; a merge onto an existing row keeps the existing values for omitted columns. A seeder that omits a NOT NULL-without-default column (the joiner's nodes row at node-registration-owner.js:154 omitting latency_assignment_state, if that column has no default) is the defect and supplies the honest value at the seeder. Justification: the cache then serves the row the authoritative table would serve; a reader can no longer observe a cache row the table could not hold. (2) Synthetic projected replicas (unified-rebalancer-replica-state.js:398-407,420-426) are not services rows and are never decoded as such: this quest introduces one named record type for a projected replica, built from decoded services rows plus the planned change, with exactly the fields replica inventory and the priority census read, in one spelling; getCurrentReplicas returns that type and its 12 call sites read the named fields. (3) Amendment confirmed: the decoders ignore exactly the cache's own declared local fields (SYSTEM_TABLE_CACHE_LOCAL_FIELD_NAMES), which stays the single declaration, pinned by a test. (4) Expectation changes confirmed: a NULL NOT NULL column refused by the decoder before the identity check; malformed steps_history refused (fail closed) instead of logged-as-empty, the refusal surfacing as a typed error never swallowed; the vacuous [undefined] assertion replaced by real statuses; the decoder refuses a wrong-typed membership_publication_epoch while the binding owner keeps refusing out-of-domain numbers: shape refusals belong to the decoder, domain refusals to the owner. (5) readOperationWorkflowRecord, normalizeOperationProgressRecord and normalizePublicationOperationWorkflowRecord are not stored-row normalisers and leave this quest's fold list; normalizeReplicaOperationRecord (18 sites) and the replica-operation-progress.js alias readers need decoding at their producers and move to system-table-decoded-reads-rebalancer. (6) Rolling upgrade is unsupported (rs-raft closeout rulings 2026-10-04): a partial row inserted by an older process is not a supported state; its refusal is correct. (7) Row naming: the group rows use underscores (control_plane); the consumer quest record system-table-decoded-reads-control-plane and the epic table on the stream are corrected to that spelling at the merge.

Round 2: lead rulings implemented (cache merge holds schema-complete rows; projected replicas as one named record type src/rebalancer/projected-replica.js returned by getCurrentReplicas; decoders ignore exactly SYSTEM_TABLE_CACHE_LOCAL_FIELD_NAMES with a pin test; services/nodes normalisers folded and deleted; 9-field planning record preserved; control_plane spelling); rows: formation_system_tables_without_decoder 0, raw reads outside decoder 1096 -> 1008 (cap 1008), alias reads 745 -> 741, state-read defaults 413 -> 402, two-source 1785 -> 1774, catch-returns-default 387 -> 386; lab reds classified except F1 (multi-node-cluster takeover) and F12 (W9 intermittent on carinas).

Lead rulings 2026-11-09 on the two open reds. F1 (join core): the sealed constraint behaviour-unchanged and the owner's join-core coupling directive bind: the cache fallback of isNodeDead must give HEAD's decision for a node row whose lease is absent (HEAD read the missing field as live and refused the duplicate id); the decoded named absent-lease state is mapped to that decision at that site with a witness (multi-node-cluster green), and the pre-existing divergence between the authoritative path (NULL = expired) and the cache fallback is routed as a finding to the join-core owner, not resolved here. F12 (W9): the witness is never weakened. Establish whether 'drive returns HELD implies all 64 targets committed' is a production guarantee: if yes, slower cache reads expose a production race, which becomes a fix quest and blocks this land until fixed or the per-target deep clone cost is removed without behaviour change; if the property is eventual and the test counts before its own in-flight targets settle, the harness observes the settled state with the justification written down. The per-target deep clone in buildSafeTargets is recorded as a performance finding for the CDC/message-group owner either way.

Round 2 F1/F12 resolution: F1 isCachedNodeRowDead maps an absent lease on the cache fallback (and the address-claim sweep) to HEAD's live-unless-terminal reading, authoritative path untouched, 3 witnesses (15/17 reverted, 17/17 with), multi-node-cluster 28/28 candidate and base; F12 classified: HELD is eventual (budget/attempts exhausted, receipts kept in the progress cell), W9 harness now re-drives withheld drives asserting HELD, same cell and strictly growing receipts on every drive, then 64 committed + 1 uncovered; observedServiceRoute reads the node row through getShared instead of a deep clone (behaviour unchanged, witness 7/8 with get restored), W9 10/10 local and 11/11 on carinas; dt6-learner-promotion fixture builds complete rows; gates 0, probe 0.

Lead rulings 2026-11-09 on the F1/F12 resolution. (1) F1 residual: before the decoders the cache fallback gave two answers for one stored state (missing lease key read live; an explicitly written NULL, the durable-rejoin reentry row, read dead); complete rows erase the key-presence distinction, so one HEAD answer must change. Ruled fail-closed: on the degraded cache-only path a row without a lease reads live, so a changed-address rejoin against a reentry-normalised non-terminal row is refused while the authoritative read is unavailable (HEAD admitted it); the authoritative path is unchanged. Flagged to the owner; the primary-vs-fallback divergence and this choice are routed to the join-core owner. (2) The dt6-learner-promotion fixture repair is confirmed (fixture partial rows under ruling 1). (3) The clone removal in observedServiceRoute is confirmed: behaviour-unchanged with a witness that the clone protected no mutation. (4) Fix-quest candidate recorded: openCdcDeliveryChildScope.run in src/cdc/cdc-delivery-invocation.js orphans the child promise when the budget expires between the two assertCurrent checks (unhandled rejection cdc_committed_acceptance_unknown); owner CDC delivery invocation. (5) Performance finding for the CDC/message-group owner: the target plan is rebuilt on every progress check (quadratic per pass).

First independent verification (Opus, scratchpad/verify-decoders/verdict.md): REJECT, 2 blocking, 5 non-blocking. Passed: 15 decoder mutations killed; 0 definitions/calls of the five normalisers in src; cache defaults match SQLite for all 44 tables; projected-replica call sites read named fields; detector groups sum to the total and the attribution rule holds by hand-check; F1 witnesses killed by reversion; W9 harness keeps the full property and the getShared witness dies under reversion; gates pass except the budget cap row. B1: system_table_raw_column_reads_outside_decoder measures 1010 > cap 1008 (two raw reads inside the new isCachedNodeRowDead), so the budget test fails. B2: complete cache rows erase the distinction between a column never observed and a stored NULL/default, and readers depend on it beyond isNodeDead: node-liveness-semantic-projection projectLease (missing = UNKNOWN, NULL = CLEARED, feeding readiness), node-readiness-policy isNodeReadyLeaseExplicitlyCleared (follow-up-move, critical-topology, move-replica-assignment-visibility), cdc-group-propagation-routing boot_incarnation ?? null (now 0 on peer hints). Non-blocking: completion refusals can throw into the CDC apply path; F7 peer-hint zeros read as observations and created_at joins last-write-wins; completion on INSERT replacement and listeners get the stored object; detector recall gaps and a latent keyColumn TypeError; sql_transactions schema/migration default mismatch.

Lead decision 2026-11-09 after the REJECT (supersedes ruling (1) of 2026-11-08 and the F1 fail-closed ruling): the cache does NOT complete rows. Completing them erased the never-observed-vs-stored-NULL distinction that readers legitimately depend on (F1 and B2 are one root: the ruling was at the wrong altitude). Instead: the cache stores exactly what was written; a seeder that writes a partial row declares a named seed projection once beside the seeder and the cache records it as a cache-local field on that row (joining SYSTEM_TABLE_CACHE_LOCAL_FIELD_NAMES, one declaration); the decoder decodes the projection's columns and gives every column outside it the named state NOT_OBSERVED, distinct from the named ABSENT state of a stored NULL; a row without a projection marker that lacks a column remains a typed refusal. Every reader that distinguished key presence (isNodeDead cache fallback and the address sweep, projectLease, isNodeReadyLeaseExplicitlyCleared, the boot_incarnation read, and any other found by census) keeps HEAD's semantics by mapping NOT_OBSERVED and ABSENT exactly as HEAD mapped missing and NULL, each with a witness that fails on reversion; the F1 residual disappears (missing reads live, explicit NULL reads dead, as at HEAD) and isCachedNodeRowDead is replaced by that mapping. The schema-default completion code, its refusal-into-CDC-apply path (non-blocking finding) and the F7 peer-hint zero values are removed with it; F7 hints become a declared seed projection. B1 (two raw reads) is fixed by decoding; caps never raised.

Round 3 (seed projections after REJECT): schema-default completion removed (cache stores exactly what was written; F-a/F-b/F-c gone; join admission files back to HEAD); four seeders declare seed projections recorded as the cache-local marker seed_projection (joiner_registration_seed, bootstrap_admission_peer_hint, priority_local_create_seed, message_group_registration_seed), marker dropped exactly when the row holds every column; decoder gives ROW_NOT_OBSERVED outside the projection and ROW_ABSENT for stored NULL; raw key-presence readers keep HEAD semantics by construction, decoded readers map through readNotObservedAsAbsent; witnesses through real seeders and a real cache, every one killed by its reversion; raw-read row 1008 within cap 1008; budget test 18/18; detector keyColumn TypeError fixed; 9 fixtures that relied on completion fixed; lab 10 reds classified (5 base-red, 3 fixed, 2 host/timing); gates 0.

Lead ruling 2026-11-09 on RD-1/RD-2: an unmarked partial row reaching the cache from a non-seeder path (a guarded CDC UPDATE whose read-back missed, sending only SET and WHERE columns to a cache that does not hold the key; the seedLocalReplicaVoterRaftRole get-then-UPSERT race) must keep HEAD semantics, not become a refusal. The cache marks any partial store of a key it does not hold with an observed-columns projection (same marker mechanism, the projection naming exactly the observed columns), so the decoder gives ROW_NOT_OBSERVED for the rest; the event is recorded as a named cache diagnostic (counted, never silent). Declared seed projections remain the owner-named form for seeders. Routed R17: the CDC read-back miss (node-lifecycle-publication.js:615, the replica_operations expecting-step family, message-group activation) to the CDC owner, and the voter raft-role race to the replica handler owner.

RD-1/RD-2 per the lead ruling: a partial store of a key the cache does not hold, on the three decoded tables and without a declared seed projection, is marked with the observed-columns projection (cache_observed_columns, exact observed columns, same marker mechanism) and counted by a named diagnostic (getObservedColumnsMarkCount, throttled warn); rowToOperation maps entityType/entityId through readNotObservedAsAbsent so a marked row is refused with HEAD's code; witnesses on real SQLite and a real cache for the RD-1 nodes and replica_operations shapes and the RD-2 race, mutation (no marking) refuses them; gates 0; budget rows unchanged within caps.

Delta verification of round 3 + RD (Opus, scratchpad/verify-decoders-r3/verdict.md): REJECT, 1 blocking, 5 non-blocking. Passed: completion gone (cache diff only the marker hook; admission files equal HEAD); 14/18 mechanism mutations killed (survivors: mark-a-held-key x2, INSERT-notifies-stored-object equivalent); raw key-presence readers byte-identical to HEAD on seeded, marked and full rows; multi-node-cluster 28/28; seeder census complete except N3; raw-read row 1008/1008, budget test 18/18; fixtures change no assertion; gates 0. B1: rowToOperation, the only decoded replica_operations reader, maps only entityType/entityId; on observed-columns rows from the real membership branch-selection CAS (replica-operation-message-group-membership-authorization.js:74, 19-column payload) it throws (decoded.stepsHistory is not iterable) where HEAD returned an operation; drop-one-column differential: 6 columns throw, the epoch gives a different refusal, 26 fields carry a Symbol where HEAD had undefined/null. Non-blocking: N1 buildPlanningServiceRecord keeps Symbols (equality-only today); N2 readServiceRecordNodeId Symbol flips one reuse decision on an unwritten shape; N3 a partial INSERT replacing a held row stays unmarked and is refused; N4 the marker counts in countPlanningEvidenceRowFields' tiebreak; N5 SystemCacheQueryService now filters by stored column names (behaviour change to state at landing).

Lead rulings 2026-11-09 for round 4: B1 is a class repair across every decoded reader of the three tables (rowToOperation, the projected replica builder, buildPlanningServiceRecord, readServiceRecordNodeId and any other consumer of decodeServicesRow/decodeNodesRow/decodeReplicaOperationsRow): each reader maps ROW_NOT_OBSERVED to exactly HEAD's reading of a missing field, field by field, from one declared per-field table per reader (undefined, null, '', [] for steps_history, HEAD's numeric parse for epoch and lease fields), never a Symbol leaking past the reader; the committed witness is the drop-one-column differential against HEAD over each table's schema for each decoded reader, plus the real membership branch-selection CAS. N1, N2 and N4 (marker excluded from field counts) are fixed in the same repair. N3: the observed-columns marker also applies when an INSERT replaces a held row with a partial payload (HEAD read the missing fields as absent there too). N5 is stated in the landing notes as an intended correction.

Round 4 (decoded-reader mapping after REJECT): defineNotObservedReading/readDecodedRow declare and apply one per-field HEAD reading table per reader (services and nodes tables follow the deleted normalisers; rowToOperation its own 37-field table); projected replicas map unobserved fields to ROW_ABSENT with two named consumer readings (readPlacementStatus, hasReplicaNode) where HEAD's consumers disagreed; N3 partial INSERT replacing a held row marked; N4 marker excluded from field counts; N5 recorded; drop-one-column differential against a frozen HEAD fixture over 16 readers (324 assertions) plus the real branch-selection CAS; 16/18 mutations killed (2 equivalent); cache/bootstrap/rebalancer/control-plane directories green; gates 0.

Lead rulings 2026-11-09 on round 4: (1) projected replicas: the consumer-side named readings are accepted, because HEAD's consumers read a missing status/node in conflicting ways and a single builder value cannot preserve all of them; each reading is named and witnessed at its consumer. (2) behaviour-unchanged binds the three differences the round-4 census listed: service_type is lower-cased where HEAD's normaliser lower-cased it; a stored '' replica_id falls back to service_id where HEAD did; and a row the decoder refuses (an unknown closed-domain value is reachable through the unvalidated register-service API) no longer fails the whole read: the refusal is per row, the row is excluded from that read and counted by a named diagnostic, never silent, never failing the other rows.

Lead rulings 2026-11-09 on round 4b: (1) the per-table refusal counter as process-wide diagnostic state is accepted (a diagnostic like a logger; not identity-keyed; threading a sink through about 40 readers adds coupling without safety). (2) Exclusion must not move a decision away from fail-closed: readEachSystemTableRow takes a per-reader declared refusal reading (exclude, or a named substitute), declared once per reader like the not-observed tables. Critical topology reads a refused nodes row as a TRANSITIONAL critical node, as HEAD did; the message-group membership debt census answers not available when a row was refused; every other converted reader is audited for the same question and declares exclude only where the row cannot change the decision toward less safe. Routed R17: the register-service HTTP API writes status/raft_role without validation (the reachable source of unknown closed-domain values), owner: management API.

Rounds 4b/4c: service_type lower-cased where HEAD did (readNormalizedServiceType, captured toLowerCase), '' replica_id falls back to service_id, per-row refusal with declared refusal readings (defineRefusalReading: exclude or substitute; readEachSystemTableRow; refusedRowCount diagnostic with throttled warn); audit: no reader may safely exclude, so every multi-row reader reads a refused row as stored (HEAD reading) except the two ruled substitutes (critical topology: refused node TRANSITIONAL; membership debt census: unavailable); the mesh-connectivity resolvers read rows as stored (lead accepts: HEAD behaviour on that path); differential 425/425 against the frozen HEAD fixture; 27/27 mutations killed; 521/522 local files green (one TAP timeout, green alone); gates 0; budget rows unchanged.

Delta verification of rounds 4-4c (Opus, scratchpad/verify-decoders-r4/verdict.md): REJECT, 1 blocking, 7 non-blocking. Passed: the HEAD fixture regenerates byte-identical from a git archive of 730225bf1; no Symbol leaks (static + walking encoder), differential 425/425; rulings implemented apart from census completeness and status case; as-stored substitute equals HEAD's reading up to case; 10 re-run mutations killed; cache/control-plane/rebalancer green, bootstrap 218/219 (load timing). B1: two replica_operations readers still call single-row rowToOperation in a loop/filter without a refusal reading (operation-workflow-replace-owner-wake.js:283-291 aborts the remote REPLACE-owner wake loop; operation-workflow-message-group-membership-recovery.js:271-276 predicate rejects the whole periodic debt sweep) where HEAD carried on. Non-blocking: N1 case-insensitive canonicalisation changes raw-compare readers for upper-case known values (unvalidated /register-service makes it reachable); N2 as-stored substitute lower-cases unknown values; N3 single-row planning reads throw (fail-closed, repeated rebuilds); N4 TRANSITIONAL substitute departs from HEAD for non-status refusals; N5 NULL edge cases in the substitute; N6 dropped HEAD guards (empty nodeId/serviceId, inventory identity branch); N7 stale comments, a nonexistent name in the notes.

Altitude check after three rejections (rounds 2, 3, 4-4c): the rejections share one root that recurs at a lower level each round: the decoder's strictness (closed-domain refusal of unknown values, case canonicalisation, completion, refusal per row) changes behaviour that HEAD's lenient normalisers and raw readers had, and every repair finds more readers. The quest's purpose is navigability under the sealed behaviour-unchanged constraint; strictness is a behaviour change. Decision: the decoders read like HEAD: every value HEAD accepted is decoded and its stored text kept (no canonicalisation inside the decoder; an unknown closed-domain value is the named UNRECOGNISED state carrying the raw value, and readers compare exactly as HEAD did); only what HEAD itself refused stays refused, plus the earlier-ruled corrupt steps_history refusal; the refusal-reading machinery that no longer has a purpose is deleted (one version, no unused code); seed and observed-columns projections, folds, projected replicas, per-field not-observed readings, the measuring rows and the B1-round-1 fixes stay. Strictness (closed-domain refusal, canonicalisation) moves to a follow-up quest paired with write-time validation of the register-service API, which changes behaviour and needs the owner's approval. The sealed statement is amended accordingly before land.
